Q27966298.summary: Seven arched niches, separated by slender columns with simple Corinthian capitals, run along this sarcophagus front. In the central niche stands a youthful, beardless Christ wearing the toga, his right hand at his breast and a scroll in his left; Peter and Paul turn toward him from the neighbouring niches, and pairs of apostles converse on either side, one of them taking a scroll from a book-box at his feet. The museum reads the central group as a variant of the Roman 'Traditio Legis', Christ giving the new Law to his apostles.
facts: The museum notes that the corner reinforcements left inside the chest when it was hollowed out are characteristic of the sarcophagi of southwestern France.
Its left short side shows Abraham about to sacrifice Isaac, a scene read by early Christians as a type of Christ's sacrifice and of salvation.
According to the museum's record it was reused in the Middle Ages to frame a church portal, so the place of its first use is unknown.
Q27966298.notes: POP: '4e quart 4e siècle ; 5e siècle'. The record names Saint-Michel-du-Touch (Toulouse) as findspot; the precise church where it was reused is only partly legible in the record as fetched. Identification of Peter and Paul follows the museum.
